input.summary: Add affiliate/successor assignment right for Sparkling and a reasonableness/no-competitor standard for Garman assignments.
input.comment: [Playbook] We added the customary carve-out allowing us to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and made consent for other assignments subject to a reasonableness standard (with no assignment by Garman to our competitors). A blanket consent requirement with no M&A carve-out would block routine group reorganisations, so we cannot accept it.

ops.oldText: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
ops.newText: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed, provided that Sparkling may assign this Agreement, without consent, to an affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, amalgamation, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or business, upon written notice to Garman, and Garman may not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Sparkling. A change of control of Sparkling shall not constitute an assignment of this Agreement and shall not give Garman any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.

ops.oldText: (c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;
ops.newText: (c) except as permitted by Section 20(d), not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;
